description: HTTP/1.1 parser and server built on top of the event loop. Implements request parsing (method, path, headers, body with Content-Length), response formatting, keep-alive connection management, and a trie-based router with dynamic segments. Exposes a native 'server' function to vek code that starts listening and dispatches requests to registered route handlers.
steps: Create src/http_parser.h - define HttpRequest struct: method (enum: GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS), path (string), query_string (string), version (HTTP/1.0 or 1.1), headers (array of key/value pairs, max 64), body (pointer+length), content_length, keep_alive flag. Define HTTP_PARSE_INCOMPLETE, HTTP_PARSE_OK, HTTP_PARSE_ERROR return codes.

Create src/http_parser.c - implement http_parse_request(buf, len, HttpRequest* out) that parses the request line and headers. Handle: CR LF line endings, header continuation (though rare), Content-Length for body. Return INCOMPLETE if not enough data yet (no double-CRLF found). This is a zero-copy parser that stores pointers into the buffer.

Create src/http_response.h/c - implement http_response_write(conn, status, headers, body) that formats a proper HTTP/1.1 response with Date header, Content-Length, Connection: keep-alive/close, and writes it to the connection's write buffer via event_loop_conn_write.

Create src/router.h - define Router struct using a trie (prefix tree). Each node has: children array (sorted by segment), handler function pointer, is_param flag, param_name. Define route_add(router, method, path, handler) and route_match(router, method, path, params_out).

Create src/router.c - implement the trie router. Split path by '/', insert segments as trie nodes. ':param' segments match any single path component and capture the value. '*' catch-all captures the rest. route_match returns the handler + a params map.

Create src/http_server.h/c - tie everything together: http_server_init(port) creates the event loop + listener, registers the on_accept callback. On data received, attempt to parse with http_parser. On complete request, call route_match to find handler, invoke handler, write response. Handle keep-alive (reset state after response for HTTP/1.1, close for 1.0 or Connection: close).

Create src/stdlib_http_server.c - expose to vek code: register native functions that let vek programs define routes and start the server. Implement: server.get(path, handler_closure), server.post(path, handler_closure), server.listen(port) that starts the event loop. The handler closure receives a request map and must return a response map (or use helper functions).

Create native request/response helpers accessible from vek: The request is exposed as an ObjMap with keys: method, path, query, headers, body, params. Response helpers: server.respond(conn, status, headers, body) or simpler: the handler returns a map {status: 200, body: 'hello', headers: {...}}.

Add integration test: tests/programs/http_hello.ve - a minimal HTTP server that responds with 'Hello, World!' on GET /. Add a test script tests/test_http.sh that starts the server in background, curls it, checks response, kills the server.
Update Makefile to have a 'test_http' target that runs the HTTP integration test
acceptance_criteria: make compiles with all HTTP-related files
A vek program can define a route handler and start listening on a port
GET requests to defined routes return correct responses with proper HTTP/1.1 formatting
Dynamic path segments (e.g., /posts/:id) are captured and available in req.params
Keep-alive connections work (multiple requests on one TCP connection)
The HTTP parser handles incomplete reads correctly (waits for more data)
make test passes all existing tests
The HTTP integration test passes (server starts, responds to curl, shuts down)
verification: Run manual HTTP test: ./build/vek run tests/programs/http_hello.ve & sleep 1 && curl -s http://localhost:3000/ && kill %1
